title: Plants
source: Piper & Beattie, Flora of the Northwest Coast (1915); Piper, Flora of the State of Washington (1906); Chesnut, Principal Poisonous Plants of the United States (USDA 1898); Pammel, A Manual of Poisonous Plants (1911)

questions.question: Growing as: a tree, a shrub, a vine, a soft-stemmed plant (herb), a fern, or grasslike?
questions.capture_condition: the whole plant is in frame
questions.citation: Piper & Beattie, Flora of the Northwest Coast (1915), habit per species description

questions.question: Leaves on the stem: alternate, opposite, whorled, or all at the base?
questions.capture_condition: a stem with several leaves is in frame
questions.citation: Piper & Beattie, Flora of the Northwest Coast (1915), leaf arrangement per species description

questions.question: Each leaf: one blade (simple), or split into leaflets (compound)?
questions.capture_condition: one full leaf fills the frame
questions.citation: Piper & Beattie, Flora of the Northwest Coast (1915), leaf form per species description

questions.question: The leaf edge: smooth (entire), toothed, or lobed?
questions.capture_condition: a leaf edge is in frame up close
questions.citation: Piper & Beattie, Flora of the Northwest Coast (1915), leaf margin per species description

questions.question: Flower color?
questions.capture_condition: an open flower is in frame in daylight
questions.citation: Piper & Beattie, Flora of the Northwest Coast (1915), flower color per species description

questions.question: Flowers sit: single (solitary), in a long cluster (raceme), in an umbrella head (umbel), in a tight head, or on a spike?
questions.capture_condition: a flowering stem is in frame
questions.citation: Piper & Beattie, Flora of the Northwest Coast (1915), inflorescence per species description

questions.question: Broken stem: milky sap, or not?
questions.citation: Pammel, A Manual of Poisonous Plants (1911), latex noted per species description

questions.question: On stems or leaves: stinging hairs, spines, or neither?
questions.capture_condition: a stem section fills the frame up close
questions.citation: Piper & Beattie, Flora of the Northwest Coast (1915), armature per species description
